verdict.root_cause: At 16:29:26 platform-automation lowered adservice's container memory limit to 256m and, unlike the four earlier apply/revert cycles in the same window, never reverted it [tr_f8569b1421de]. Within ~20 seconds adservice stops serving requests and begins repeating a JVM/OTel startup banner seven times with geometrically lengthening gaps - a container killed during JVM initialization and restarted under supervisor backoff, never reaching a gRPC listening state [tr_d369b4d0ec9f]. With no ad backend endpoint bound, frontend fails at connection setup: gRPC code 14 UNAVAILABLE with 'no connection established' [tr_764cb8a15010], and the only error-bearing traces bottom out in a frontend-side tcp.connect (~3.06s) under AdService/GetAds with no adservice server span at all [tr_51a83bb19688]. All other frontend routes are healthy, which is why damage is partial and bursty [tr_9fa1c42d9f11].
verdict.reasoning: Timing, mechanism and caller symptom converge. The only unreverted change in the blast radius lands three minutes before adservice's transition from serving to restart-looping [tr_f8569b1421de, tr_d369b4d0ec9f]. Lengthening restart gaps with no server-ready line is a crash loop, not a deploy or drain [tr_d369b4d0ec9f]. Frontend's failure is transport-level - connection never established, deepest span a frontend-side tcp.connect with no adservice server span - exactly what a callee with no listening endpoint produces, explaining why frontend alerted while the fault is one hop down [tr_764cb8a15010, tr_51a83bb19688]. I class this resource_exhaustion, not bad_config: the limit edit is how it started; being killed for exceeding available memory is what is happening. Alternatives close out - no changes on frontend or productcatalogservice [tr_8c933b789e58], cartservice's chaos actions were all reverted hours before onset [tr_1e5a2f5c8626], and cart/catalog/currency/shipping/payment/email legs are fast and error-free [tr_51a83bb19688]. Restoring the prior memory limit is the fix, since four earlier cycles show adservice serves fine under it.
open_questions: No direct kill evidence: no OOMKilled event, exit code 137, or JVM OutOfMemoryError was observed, and that negative sits on a truncated log result [tr_d369b4d0ec9f]. Memory saturation and restart-count metrics for adservice were never queried [tr_1b0cbf96a106].

Frontend gRPC errors appear from ~15:48 [tr_764cb8a15010], before the 16:29 adservice transition; whether those are the same fault, another callee, or noise is unresolved since the log lines name no target.

Frontend's error ratio dips to zero and peaks near 37% [tr_9fa1c42d9f11] rather than failing the ad branch consistently; the source of that intermittency, the unmeasured edge triage flagged, and loadgenerator's earlier alert were never investigated.

alternatives.root_cause: adservice crash-loops for a reason internal to its startup (agent incompatibility, corrupt state, init-time dependency failure) and the memory-limit change three minutes earlier is coincidental.
alternatives.why_not: The four prior apply/revert cycles show adservice starts fine without the constraint, and the transition follows the unreverted apply by ~20 seconds; no startup exception or bind failure appears in the returned lines [tr_f8569b1421de, tr_d369b4d0ec9f].

alternatives.root_cause: A cluster-level networking or service-discovery fault makes the adservice endpoint unreachable from frontend while adservice itself is fine.
alternatives.why_not: adservice's own logs show it not serving any request after ~16:29:23 [tr_d369b4d0ec9f], so unreachability is explained at the callee; a network-only fault would not produce a restart loop in the backend.

proposal.expected_effect: Removing the 256m memory limit applied at 16:29:26 and never reverted should let the JVM finish init. In Loki {service="ad-service"}: the startup banner stops repeating (backoff ladder ends) and 'received ad request' lines resume within ~90s. Frontend's 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established' lines cease and its error ratio settles near 0; AdService/GetAds traces show an adservice server span instead of a ~3.06s frontend tcp.connect.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if after 5 minutes the banner still repeats with no request lines — the kill cause would not be the memory cap, since no OOMKilled event, exit 137, or OutOfMemoryError was observed and that negative rests on a truncated log [tr_d369b4d0ec9f]. Partially falsified if adservice recovers but frontend still logs code 14, since those errors predate 16:29 and name no target. Also falsified if platform-automation re-applies the 256m limit and the loop returns.
proposal.risk: Removes a memory guardrail: if adservice actually leaks, it now grows unbounded and can pressure co-located containers instead of crash-looping. Recreate discards in-process cache and resets backoff. If the real cause is a JVM/agent or image fault, this spends the config-revert lever and leaves the loop running. Automation owns all nine changes here and may overwrite the revert, causing flapping.
proposal.blast_radius: adservice recreated; frontend (its only inbound caller) sees resets during recreate — no worse than the current total absence of a listener. loadgenerator sees ad-branch requests change; other frontend routes are unaffected.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity with frontend alerting alongside the load generator points to real user-facing impact, not a lone synthetic signal. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts alone don't distinguish a bad deploy from a slow downstream dependency.
